passages.original: AERIS in campis, memorat quos musa Maronis, 1
passages.english: In the fields of air, which the Muse of Maro recalls,
passages.notes: The trailing "1" is a line number from the edition and has been omitted. "Maro" is Virgil (Publius Vergilius Maro); the "fields of air" (aeris campi) echo his description of the underworld in Aeneid 6. The opening of Ausonius' Cupid Crucified.
